verdicts.evidence: committedTasks in skeleton.go implements exactly the three-source fallback chain (event's own tasks list, then close record ids regardless of status, then wave_dispatched event), and TestBuildShippedDerivesTasksForAnEmptyCommitList covers all four outcomes (event list wins, close record, dispatch fallback, dash) plus TestBuildShippedFallbackMatchesTheWholeDispatchKey pins the (wave,slice,attempt) key matching. The 8th golden (waivedWaveDoc) shows the shipped row '4 — Rename the field; 5 — Backfill the old rows' derived from a close record whose task 4 sits at pre-waiver status 'rework'. go test ./internal/finish/... passes (all tests including these green).

TestWaveTimingsLastCloseWins builds an event log with a wave closed twice under the same (wave,slice,attempt) key and asserts exactly one span for it (last close wins), alongside a reworked wave's two attempts and a two-slice wave, each producing separate spans (4 spans total for 3 distinct waves/keys). Test passes under go test ./internal/finish/.... The waivedWaveDoc golden's Numbers block also holds one wave_timings entry for the re-closed wave.

skeleton_test.go's TestRenderSkeletonGolden table has exactly 8 entries, the 8th named 'waived wave' using waivedWaveIn()/waivedWaveEx(); the waivedWave() helper explicitly builds these via finish.BuildRetroInputs and finish.BuildShipped, not hand-written. go test ./internal/finish/... passes (verified directly, all tests PASS including TestRenderSkeletonGolden).

BuildPR in pr.go inserts issuesSection(...) between goalsSection (## Goals) and the ## Run section; issueRefs recognizes bare #N, https?://.../issues/N URLs, and owner/repo#N cross-repo tokens, de-duplicated in topic order, with the keyword 'Closes'/'closes' repeated per reference, and issuesSection returns empty when no refs are found. TestBuildPRIssuesSection is table-driven over none/one/several/'#49 item 1'/an issue URL/a cross-repo token/a mix of forms, and assertIssuesSection asserts the closing-keyword count equals len(want). All finish tests pass.

Both commands/takt.md and hosts/copilot/skills/takt/SKILL.md contain the identical sentence 'the `push_pr` run op, and an `archived` stop's `cleanup` commands once the user has confirmed them', attaching the push-and-branch exception to those two ops. crossHostInvariants in prompt_test.go anchors this exact clause and TestPromptInvariantsReadTheSameOnEveryHost checks both files against it. go test ./internal/prompt/... passes (verified directly, all PASS).

task hosts:gen was run and produced no diff to hosts/copilot/skills/takt/SKILL.md (byte-for-byte reproduction), and task hosts:check exits 0. RenderCopilotSkill in internal/hosts/skill.go applies an ordered profile of substitutions (copilotSkillProfile), each declaring an exact expected match count, injecting the plugin manifest version into the handshake substitution, and erroring by name when a from text's count does not match. TestRenderCopilotSkillErrorsWhenARegionDoesNotMatchItsCount covers both the zero-match ('matched 0 times, declared 1') and multi-match ('matched 2 times, declared 1') cases. go test ./internal/hosts/... ./internal/tools/hostgen/... passes.

grep -rn plainOp --include='*.go' . and grep for plainOp in the design doc both find nothing. archive.go's applyAndStop comment now says every caller 'reaches here holding the lock' (not 'takes no lock'), and design §7.5 step 5 states 'commit `takt(<slug>): archive` — the last commit the archive step takes' (scoped to the step, not the run) plus 'a post-archive `takt retro --rewrite` plus `done --step retro` lands a `takt(<slug>): retro done` bundle commit'. doneRetro's comment in cmd_done.go cites 'design §7.5 step 5 names the post-archive `retro done` commit this records', pointing at that same passage. Neither archive.go nor the design doc contains 'run's last' as a naming of the archive commit.

Design §5.1's `takt retro --rewrite` row states 'a live holder fails the command outright, naming the holder and its heartbeat, with a hint to `takt unlock` — rather than the `ask: owner` gate §4.6 describes for `next`'. cmdRetro's lockBlocked callback in cmd_retro.go does exactly this: it fails with 'the run is held by '+held.ID+' (heartbeat '+held.Heartbeat.Format(time.RFC3339)+')' and hints 'run `takt unlock --slug <slug>`'.

follow_ups.title: Copilot host files section still describes the skill as hand-kept except for its version line
follow_ups.detail: CONTRIBUTING.md:67-71 ("### Copilot host files") says only "`hosts/copilot/agents/*.agent.md` are generated from `agents/*.md` by `task hosts:gen`... The skill's `takt version --expect <version>` line is stamped by `task version:set`" — implying the rest of hosts/copilot/skills/takt/SKILL.md is hand-maintained. This diff (internal/hosts/skill.go, internal/tools/hostgen/main.go's generateSkill) makes the WHOLE skill file a render of commands/takt.md via a substitution profile, written and staleness-checked by the same `task hosts:gen` / `task hosts:check` that already covers the agent files (per the new TestRunRegeneratesAHandEditedSkill and TestRunRefusesARootMissingASkillSource). A contributor following this section would still believe hand-editing the skill body is normal practice and that only the version line is generator-owned, which is no longer true and will now be silently overwritten by `task hosts:gen` or fail `task hosts:check`/CI.

follow_ups.title: Design doc's §14 testing table and §3.3/§6.1 architecture text omit the new skill-generation parity test and its "generated, never hand-edited" status
follow_ups.detail: Line 1239 (§14 Testing table, `prompt` row) names the Copilot parity tests by name — `TestCopilotSkillNamesEverythingTheBinaryCanEmit`, `TestCopilotSkillHandshakeMatchesTheManifest`, `TestCopilotAgentsAreGeneratedFromTheClaudeCodeAgents`, `TestCopilotHostFrontmatterIsParseable` — but not the new `TestCopilotSkillIsGeneratedFromTheClaudeCodePrompt` (internal/prompt/copilot_test.go) that proves the skill is a byte-exact render of commands/takt.md, the direct skill-level analogue of the agents' own parity test already listed. Two related spots are stale the same way: §3.3's repository-layout table (lines 111-112) marks `hosts/copilot/agents/*.agent.md` "generated from agents/*.md — never hand-edited" but leaves the SKILL.md row (line 111) and the internal/hosts and internal/tools/hostgen rows (lines 128-130, "renders agents/*.md for other hosts" / "writes and checks the generated Copilot agent files") not mentioning the skill at all; and §6.1's paragraph (lines 611-616) ends "...fail when a generated agent file is stale" without now also covering the generated skill file. None of these were touched by this diff even though the diff is exactly the change (#66/§2.3) that makes them incomplete.

follow_ups.title: Slice-floor-to-1 rule hand-duplicated between timingKeyOf and closeKeyOf
follow_ups.detail: timingKeyOf (line 309: `max(int(sl), 1)`) and the new closeKeyOf (line 317: `max(c.Slice, 1)`) encode the same 'floor a missing/zero slice to 1' rule inline in two places rather than through one named helper (e.g. `floorSlice(n int) int`). closeKeyOf's own doc comment even says it floors 'the way [timingKeyOf] floors', which is a hint the two could share one function instead of restating the rule.

follow_ups.title: TestWaveTimingsLastCloseWins cannot distinguish "last in log order" from "latest timestamp"
follow_ups.detail: The fixture's two wave_closed events sharing a key are appended to the events slice in the same order as their timestamps (5min then 8min), so the map-overwrite behaviour documented at internal/finish/retro.go:335-340 ('the LAST one in log order wins') is indistinguishable, by this test, from an implementation that instead picked the later-timestamped close. A fixture that puts the earlier-timestamped close event after the later one in the slice (log order diverging from timestamp order) would pin the documented rule rather than a coincidentally-equivalent one.

follow_ups.title: No test proves the close record wins over a co-present, differently-tasked wave_dispatched fallback
follow_ups.detail: committedTasks (internal/finish/skeleton.go) tries the event's own list, then the close record, then the dispatch event, in that order. TestBuildShippedFallbackMatchesTheWholeDispatchKey's 'a matching record with no tasks falls through to the dispatch' case (skeleton_test.go:377) only shows the close-record-empty → dispatch-fallback transition; TestBuildShippedDerivesTasksForAnEmptyCommitList's 'an empty list takes the ids of the close record' case has no dispatch event present at all. No case has both a matching, non-empty close record and a matching, differently-tasked wave_dispatched event in the same fixture, so priority order 2-over-3 is never directly demonstrated (it currently follows from the early-return control flow, but that flow is not itself pinned by a test).

follow_ups.title: No test proves isWordByte's non-ASCII boundary claim
follow_ups.detail: isWordByte's doc comment (pr.go:220-221) states 'A byte of a multi-byte rune is not one, so a topic written in another script still names its issue' — an explicit, testable claim about UTF-8 continuation bytes never matching the word-byte check. No case in TestBuildPRIssuesSection (pr_test.go:192) puts a non-ASCII character immediately before or after a bare '#N' reference to verify that claim.

follow_ups.title: Bare-#N leading-boundary negatives cover only letters and slash, not digits or underscore
follow_ups.detail: isWordByte (internal/finish/pr.go:222) treats '_', digits and ASCII letters alike as word bytes, and bareRefIsBounded (pr.go:210) uses it to reject a preceding word byte. TestBuildPRIssuesSection's leading-boundary negatives are 'abc#71', 'takt#71' (letters), '/#71' and 'owner/#71' (slash) — no case precedes '#' with a digit or '_', so those two branches of isWordByte are exercised only redundantly through the letter cases, never distinguished from them.

follow_ups.title: substitutionLabel's truncation branch is never exercised
follow_ups.detail: substitutionLabel truncates a from region to labelMax (56) runes at line 153-154, but every case in TestRenderCopilotSkillErrorsWhenARegionDoesNotMatchItsCount (internal/hosts/skill_test.go) breaks the H1 substitution, whose from text ('# /takt — the op loop', 22 runes) never approaches 56. The frontmatter substitution's from field is far longer than 56 runes, so the truncation path this function exists for is never hit by a test.

follow_ups.title: generateSkill duplicates the agent loop's compare/check/write logic instead of sharing a helper
follow_ups.detail: run()'s per-agent loop (lines 66-78: read dst, bytes.Equal skip, `check` → print "stale:" + count, else write() + print "wrote") is the same four-branch shape newly written again in generateSkill (lines 117-127) for the skill file. Both were touched/added by this wave's task-3. A small `writeOrReport(dst, out, check, stdout, stderr) (stale int, err error)` would serve both call sites; instead the diff reimplements the pattern rather than factoring it, which is exactly the 'duplicated helper' this lens looks for — and it is the same file, so a future edit to one copy (e.g. the stale-message wording) can silently drift from the other.

follow_ups.title: manifestVersion names a function here but a struct/type for the same concept elsewhere in the codebase
follow_ups.detail: internal/tools/hostgen/main.go:136 introduces `func manifestVersion(path string) (string, error)`, and internal/prompt/copilot_test.go:100 (this same wave) introduces a same-named test helper function. internal/cli/cmd_version.go:88 already has `type manifestVersion struct { Version string }` for the identical concept (the plugin manifest's version field). Different packages so it compiles, but the same identifier names a type in one place and a function in two others for what the brief itself treats as one recurring concept (spec §2.3's handshake version).

follow_ups.title: manifestVersion's JSON-unmarshal and empty-version error returns are untested
follow_ups.detail: manifestVersion (main.go:136-151) has three error returns: file-read failure, json.Unmarshal failure (line 144-146), and an empty "version" field (line 147-149). Only the file-read failure is exercised, via TestRunRefusesARootMissingASkillSource's 'no manifest' case (main_test.go:177), which removes the file rather than corrupting or emptying its version. The other two returns are never triggered by any test.

follow_ups.title: Missing-version-field error reads differently from the CLI's own phrasing for the same condition
follow_ups.detail: hostgen's manifestVersion renders a missing/empty "version" field as `fmt.Errorf("%s: no \"version\" field", path)` (internal/tools/hostgen/main.go:148), while internal/cli/cmd_version.go:139 renders the identical condition — an empty version in the same .claude-plugin/plugin.json — as `"plugin manifest " + path + " has no version field"`. Same fact, two different sentence shapes and quoting conventions for the one JSON field this wave's task-3 cares about (§2.3's version handshake).

follow_ups.title: generateSkill's RenderCopilotSkill error path (a render error is exitFailure) is never exercised
follow_ups.detail: internal/tools/hostgen/main.go:112-115 returns the error from hosts.RenderCopilotSkill straight out of generateSkill, and run() (main.go:85-89) turns it into exitFailure — spec §2.3 explicitly names this half of the contract ('a render error is exitFailure'). Neither TestRunRegeneratesAHandEditedSkill nor TestRunRefusesARootMissingASkillSource (nor any other test in main_test.go) ever seeds a root whose commands/takt.md fails a substitution's declared count, so this branch of generateSkill/run is untested at the hostgen level — it is only exercised indirectly through hosts.RenderCopilotSkill's own unit tests in internal/hosts/skill_test.go, never through run()'s wiring of that error into exitFailure and its stderr message.

follow_ups.title: Test failure strings still use the retired "run's last" framing this task eliminates elsewhere
follow_ups.detail: archive_test.go:177 ("the archive commit is the run's last write") and archive_test.go:327 ("keep is applied by the archive commit, which is the run's last write") still phrase the invariant in exactly the terms G7 retires from archive.go and the design doc ("the run's last …"). archive_test.go isn't one of task-4's editable files, so this isn't something the implementer could fix here, but it's now the one place in internal/cli that still asserts the archive commit is "the run's last write" — a claim the rest of the package and the design doc now go out of their way not to make, since a post-archive `retro --rewrite` + `done --step retro` can land a later commit. Worth a follow-up cleanup so the test vocabulary matches the comments it exercises.
